summary: This lecture opens the second season of the Prophet's story, the first revelation. The ustaz recalls the rebuilding of the Kaaba, then explains that at 35 to 38 he was wealthy and well known but grieved by the ignorance around him, such as burying baby girls and oppressing the poor. He began withdrawing to the Cave of Hira on Jabal Nur, supplied by Khadijah, for six months seeing dreams that came true and hearing a stone give greetings. On a Monday night in Ramadan, Jibril embraced him three times and recited the opening of Surah Al-Alaq. He ran home frightened, asked to be covered, and said he feared he was possessed by a jinn. The ustaz closes by promising the story of a blind man who will explain what happened.
keyPoints: The second season of the Prophet's story begins with the first revelation, sent down in Ramadan.
Seeing the ignorance around him, he began withdrawing to the Cave of Hira on Jabal Nur and Khadijah sent supplies.
For six months his dreams came true, one of forty-six parts of revelation.
Jibril embraced him three times and recited Iqra' bismi rabbika, and he memorised the verses.
He returned frightened and Khadijah covered him without asking, while he worried he was possessed.

chapters.title: Opening and recap of the Kaaba
chapters.summary: After a long break the ustaz recalls the Kaaba, the Black Stone and Muhammad Al-Amin.

chapters.title: Season two: revelation begins
chapters.summary: The ustaz says season one ended at 35, and season two begins with the Quran's descent in Ramadan. The house of the Prophet and Khadijah was found again underground.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW is well known and helps the poor
chapters.summary: He was rich and well known, and the tent in front of his house gave food to the poor.

chapters.title: The evils of ignorance
chapters.summary: He grieved to see baby girls buried alive and the poor oppressed with nowhere to complain.

chapters.title: He withdraws seeking guidance
chapters.summary: At 38 he wanted solitude to seek guidance on how humans should live well.

chapters.title: Jabal Nur and the Cave of Hira
chapters.summary: He climbed the hill now called Jabal Nur to a small cave that fits one person, carrying simple provisions.

chapters.title: Tahannuth and Khadijah's supplies
chapters.summary: He reflected on the state of mankind for days, and Khadijah herself climbed up with supplies.

chapters.title: Dreams that came true
chapters.summary: For six months, starting in Rabi' al-Awwal, his dreams came true the next day.

chapters.title: Three kinds of dreams
chapters.summary: Dreams may come from Allah, Satan or one's own thoughts, so recite Ayat al-Kursi and the three Quls before sleeping.

chapters.title: The stone gives greetings
chapters.summary: He said he knew a stone in Mecca that greeted him before prophethood.

chapters.title: The night of the first revelation
chapters.summary: Some scholars say the night of 21 Ramadan, a Monday. He was brave being alone in the cave.

chapters.title: Jibril embraces him
chapters.summary: Jibril descended in his true form and embraced him very tightly.

chapters.title: Read, and the memory of the Arabs
chapters.summary: Jibril said read and he replied that he could not read. The ustaz explains the Arabs' famous memory, as with Imam Shafi'i.

chapters.title: The third embrace and the first verses
chapters.summary: After the third embrace Jibril recited the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq and he memorised them at once.

chapters.title: Running home to Khadijah
chapters.summary: He ran down the hill and asked to be covered, and Khadijah held him without asking.

chapters.title: I fear I am possessed
chapters.summary: He feared being possessed because he did not yet know who had embraced him, and the story continues next week.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites the first verse of Surah Al-Alaq delivered by Jibril.
dalil.translation: Read! In the name of your Lord who created:

dalil.context: He created man from a clinging clot.
dalil.translation: He created manfrom a clinging form.

dalil.context: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.
dalil.translation: Read! Your Lord is the Most Bountiful One
who taught by [means of] the pen,

dalil.context: Taught man what he did not know.
dalil.translation: who taught man what he did not know.

dalil.context: The ustaz refers to the verse in Surah Ad-Duha that Allah found him searching and guided him.
dalil.translation: Did He not find you lost and guide you?
The Prophet SAW said a good dream is one of forty-six parts of prophethood or revelation.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites the Prophet's words when explaining the six months of dreams. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said he knew a stone in Mecca that gave him greetings before he was sent.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites the Prophet's words as one of the signs of preparation for prophethood. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW related that the angel embraced him three times and told him to read, then he returned trembling and asked to be covered.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates the first revelation as it is reported. He does not name a narrator or source.

books.context: A sirah summary covering the beginning of revelation in the Cave of Hira.

people.context: Mentioned because the Prophet SAW was known as his grandson.
The architect called to rebuild the Kaaba.
Climbed the hill to deliver supplies and covered him without asking.
Descended in his true form, embraced him three times and recited the first verses of Al-Alaq.
Mentioned as an example of someone who memorised millions of hadiths.

people.role: Imam of a school of law
people.context: His memory was so strong that reading once sufficed, and he memorised the Quran as a child.

sirah.era: The start of revelation: the Cave of Hira
sirah.summary: This lecture covers age 35 to about 40, from the rebuilding of the Kaaba to the first revelation in the Cave of Hira and his return to Khadijah.

events.title: He begins to seclude himself
events.desc: At 38 he sought guidance through seclusion.

events.label: Cave of Hira
events.title: Retreating in the Cave of Hira

events.label: Dreams
events.title: Dreams that come true

lessons.title: Seeking guidance
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW withdrew because he wanted guidance on how people should live well.

lessons.title: Helping the poor
lessons.body: Though rich and famous, the Prophet SAW always helped those in difficulty in Mecca.

lessons.title: Reflection and purposeful solitude
lessons.body: He reflected on the condition of mankind and sought the right path.

lessons.title: Supporting one's spouse
lessons.body: Khadijah climbed to bring supplies and covered him without questioning.

lessons.title: Three kinds of dreams
lessons.body: Dreams may come from Allah, Satan or our own thoughts, so make wudu and read Ayat al-Kursi before sleeping.

lessons.title: Angels guard those who recite
lessons.body: One who recites Ayat al-Kursi and the three Quls before sleeping is guarded by angels until morning.

lessons.title: Allah prepares His prophet
lessons.body: True dreams and the stone's greeting were signs of preparation before revelation.

lessons.title: Reading in the name of the Lord
lessons.body: The first revelation commanded reading in the name of the Lord who created.

lessons.title: The Arabs' strength of memory
lessons.body: The Arabs memorised lineages and poems, so they could memorise the Quran easily.

lessons.title: Revelation came in Ramadan
lessons.body: The Quran began to descend in Ramadan, possibly on an odd night such as the 21st.
